reviewFindings.summary: InfernalWallNavmesh35.Release() disabled the native grid cut and then threw before _released, visual cleanup, QueueGridRestore and reference cleanup, while both InfernalWallRules35 callers had already set a one-way breach/retire flag, so an interrupted release stranded navigation claims and the section lifetime and permanently skipped the residual cold and fire fog.
reviewFindings.reachability: Reachable, not refuted: HandlePartyLeaveArea retires on area transition, exactly when AstarPath.active can already have been replaced.
reviewFindings.engineContract: Pathfinding.GridGraph.UpdateArea clears GraphUpdateObject.updating as its final act, so an in-flight update is transient and a replaced graph is terminal.
reviewFindings.repair: Retirement plans one step at a time: defer and resume for an in-flight update, complete without a native revert for a replaced graph or absent revert pair, otherwise submit the paired revert. Forced completion on destruction and a bounded defer budget prevent stranded ownership; consequences run in a finally so they occur exactly once.

nativeRegression.kind: controlled native regression: the engine updating flag was supplied and then cleared by the fixture in place of GridGraph.UpdateArea; the deferral, resumption and all cleanup observed are the production retirement code executing natively
nativeRegression.notANaturalRace: This exercises the production retirement path under a fixture-induced precondition. It is not an observation of a naturally occurring engine race.
